# Third-Party Release Materials

This directory contains license texts and source materials that accompany the
prebuilt files distributed with S2P-XInput-Lite. It supplements
`THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`; it does not replace the original upstream licenses.

## esptool 4.11.0

The bundled Windows executable is the unmodified `esptool.exe` extracted from
Espressif's official `esptool-v4.11.0-windows-amd64.zip` release asset.

- Upstream release: https://github.com/espressif/esptool/releases/tag/v4.11.0
- Upstream tag commit: `fd42239ccc17ee244aeb1d6a1b870700894d0199`
- Official Windows archive SHA-256:
  `0EDAB659CCA62DF69C91A80CC685C1C3BBDEFB7EFF53ABF43C2B902A735AD2F9`
- Bundled `esptool.exe` SHA-256:
  `71B8C5E129A44E26851BD8E59DC8D299A1EB07BBD445A8E0A49ED64A0444ED1A`
- Accompanying source archive SHA-256:
  `18B07BF6307C659A7752F81113C4EBFF56F656B95FDB4D08296240E4A6030793`
- License: `licenses/esptool-4.11.0/LICENSE`
- Upstream README: `licenses/esptool-4.11.0/UPSTREAM_README.md`
- Complete tagged source: `sources/esptool-v4.11.0-source.zip`

The source archive is generated by GitHub from the exact upstream `v4.11.0`
tag and is distributed next to the executable so recipients do not have to
depend on a moving external link to obtain the corresponding source.

## ESP32-S3 firmware dependencies

The firmware dependency lock records these exact build inputs:

- ESP-IDF 5.5.4, Apache License 2.0 (`licenses/esp-idf-5.5.4`)
- Espressif ESP TinyUSB 1.7.6~2, Apache License 2.0
  (`licenses/esp-tinyusb-1.7.6`)
- TinyUSB 0.19.0~3, MIT License (`licenses/tinyusb-0.19.0`)
- Fusion AHRS 1.2.11, MIT License (`licenses/fusion-1.2.11`)

Their retained license texts are under `licenses/`. Complete S2P firmware
source and the component lock are in
`esp32s3/source/esp32s3_usb_bridge_bluedroid` in the repository source release.

The standalone XInput implementation also incorporates or adapts portions of
these MIT-licensed reference implementations:

- Adafruit TinyUSB XInput, audited at commit
  `4b5617b19294e808ce1d950a69e6e5cc96f4ec06`
- GP2040-CE, audited at commit
  `5fb6404d3467ea1c55730d2e39446fafbb2df26a`

Their copyright and permission notices are retained under `licenses/`.

## Portable Python runtime

Python and installed Python packages retain their upstream metadata and
license files inside `runtime` and each package's `.dist-info` directory. The
upstream pyserial 3.5 and PyWinRT 3.2.1 wheels omit their standalone license
files, so the release builder restores the exact tag-specific license text
from `licenses/pyserial-3.5` and `licenses/pywinrt-3.2.1` into the relevant
`.dist-info` directories. The pinned package versions are listed in
`src/requirements.txt` and `src/requirements-binary.txt`.
